title: The same sentence costs 3x more in Hindi
sources: Universal Declaration of Human Rights, Article 1 (parallel text)

beats.say: This sentence costs three times more in Hindi than in English.
beats.cap: This sentence costs 3× more in Hindi

beats.say: Language models do not read letters. They read bytes.
beats.cap: Models don't read letters — they read bytes

beats.say: In U T F eight, a Latin letter is one byte. An accented one is two. A Japanese character is three.
beats.cap: UTF-8: Latin is 1 byte, accented 2, Japanese 3

beats.say: So I measured the same paragraph in eight languages.
Turkish, one hundred seventy one. Basically free.
But Japanese is the strange one.
beats.cap: But Japanese is the strange one

beats.say: Three bytes per character. The highest of all of them.
It still lands at one point five times English.
Because it says the same thing in half the characters.
beats.cap: It says the same thing in half the characters

beats.say: It is not the language that costs more. It is the alphabet.
beats.cap: It's not the language. It's the alphabet.
